as_told.title: Doty reportedly confessed to forging the Ellsworth document

plain: There is a supposed Air Force document saying that on November 16, 1977, guards at a missile site called L9, near Ellsworth Air Force Base in South Dakota, were attacked with a beam by aliens. The UFO historian Richard Dolan mentions it in passing, saying it is a document "which has been manipulated" and that it was traced back to Richard Doty, a former Air Force investigator. Michels covers it in more detail in an episode with Air Force veterans who say they were abducted. He gives the date and the L9 site, and he credits the UFO researcher Brad Sparks for work on the case. He also passes on a chain of reports: according to the physicist and UFO researcher Bruce Maccabee, the researcher Bill Moore said that Doty confessed to forging the Ellsworth document. So the tellers differ on how far it goes, from a document that was altered to an outright forgery. It matters because a fake official record can steer UFO research the wrong way for years.
